title: Coalesce ops sketchpad — week of 2028-12-05
notes:
Context:
This is a lightweight ops sketchpad from the weekly sync focused on coalescing, KV shadowing, and kernel-level batching tweaks. Goal is to capture what we tried, immediate observations, and short actionable next steps. Not a polished playbook — intentionally rough.

Attendees:
- Maya (owner)
- Arjun
- Lina
- Samir
- Pavel (observability drop-in)

Quick metrics snapshot (baseline vs experiment run):
- p50 generation latency (hosted, 512 tokens): baseline 82ms -> experiment 74ms
- p95: baseline 210ms -> experiment 198ms
- tokens/sec (steady-state batch): baseline 43k -> experiment 51k (+18%)
- KV-cache hit-rate (synthetic prefix set): baseline 61% -> experiment 76%
- Observed tail GC-like stalls: 0 in experiment runs (was intermittent on baseline)

What we changed this week (high level):
1) Coalescer: adjusted max-coalesce-window from 8ms -> 6ms and lowered stall-threshold to 2ms. Rationale: recent traffic patterns show short bursts; shorter window reduced burst amplification under low-concurrency clients.
2) KV shadowing: enabled async shadow-populate for a subset of routes (route tags: /chat/long-history). Shadow writes go to a local LRU-16k buffer and mirrored to main cache on success.
3) Kernel scheduling: introduced a microbatch affinity hint to encourage kernels to keep prefetched KV slices co-located; this reduces cross-kernel NVLink transfers in multi-GPU hosts.

Experiment setup notes:
- Traffic: replay of prod trace sample from 2028-11-28 (10% slice) with synthetic cold-starts inserted at 1-in-100 requests to exercise KV-populate code path.
- Cluster: dedicated CI fleet (4x A100-80GB nodes, same as canary pool).
- Version: PR 1891 applied; runtime flag --coalesce-window-ms=6; --kv-shadow-async=true.
- Observability: additional tracing enabled for 'coalesce.decision' and 'kv.shadow.write' spans; temporary dashboards created in Grafana panel kit 'ops/maya/coalesce-weekly'.

Observations & notes (raw):
- Coalesce window reduction tightened latency on short queries but increased the number of kernel launches per second by ~9%. Net cost per-token still improved because batching was higher-quality (less straggler amplification).
- Async KV shadowing significantly improved cold-start latency for long-history routes; hit-rate improvement concentrated in users with >3 prior turns.
- Microbatch affinity reduced NVLink cross-shard copies by ~22% in the replay, but we observed two edge cases where affinity pinned small batches to already-hot nodes causing thermal throttling in long runs. Need thermal-safe backoff.
- One regression: under a spike template (simulated 3x arrival rate for 30s), the new coalescer caused a short-lived admission burst where several >32-token requests were coalesced together, producing a single very long microbatch and causing p95 to spike by ~120ms for unrelated short queries. We need a max-aggregate-token cap per-coalesce-window.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Add max-aggregate-token cap to coalescer (owner: Arjun, due: 2028-12-08).
- Implement thermal backoff for microbatch affinity hint (owner: Lina, due: 2028-12-11).
- Run extended 24h soak with traffic mix including 2% heavy-chat and flash-spike templates (owner: Samir, due: 2028-12-12).
- Add KV-shadow failure telemetry (owner: Maya, due: 2028-12-07) — track write latency and dropped shadow writes.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Safety of async shadow-populate for regulated routes: Paul from security asked if writes to shadow buffer count as persistent storage; we need a short note from security to clarify compliance implications. (Ping: Paul)
- Backpressure integration: should coalescer signal backpressure when aggregate tokens exceed adjustable threshold or let kernel admission handle it? Current leaning: coalescer should be first gate to avoid creating huge microbatches.
- Rollout plan: can we do staged rollout by route tag? Yes — Lina proposes route-tag-based feature flags in edge-router and runtime checks. Implementation cost estimate: 2d infra + 1d runtime changes.

Decisions made this week:
- Short-term: accept coalescer window=6ms for canary pool; add max-aggregate-token cap before broader rollout.
- Medium-term: continue with async KV-shadow for long-history routes and add telemetry windows for shadow write latency and errors.

Incidents / Postmortem notes:
- No incidents in production this week tied to these experiments. One CI run tripped on thermal policy as noted above; CI machine recovered and test resumed.

Notes to self / rough todos:
- Sketch a small diagram for coalescer decision path (if request.size + current-window.tokens > cap -> flush; else coalesce). Rough ascii okay for next sync.
- Add unit tests around coalesce aggregation and eviction interplay with KV-prefill (Arjun + Samir pairing).

Next sync agenda (2028-12-12):
- Review soak results and new telemetry from KV-shadow
- Arjun: demo max-aggregate-token cap behavior in CI
- Lina: present thermal backoff design for affinity hints
- Decide rollout gating metrics and abort criteria (target: p95 unchanged within +/-50ms and token-cost delta < 8%)

References / quick links:
- Linear ticket: REDW-1423 (coalescer aggregate cap)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1891 (coalesce + kv-shadow)
- Grafana: ops/maya/coalesce-weekly (private)

Random scribbles: 
- 'If we cap aggregate tokens at 256 per-window, short queries remain low-latency, and heavy requests will still batch across windows' — test with 256/128/512 knob sweep.
- Consider a 'soft-throttle' that probabilistically rejects coalescing when thermal headroom low (lighter hammer than full backoff).

End of sketchpad. Will convert key parts to a short playbook once action items land and soak looks stable.
summary: Weekly ops sketch capturing a canary-run of tightened coalescing windows, async KV shadowing for long-history routes, and a microbatch affinity hint experiment. Found latency improvements and an edge-case that requires a max-aggregate-token cap; action items assigned.
